interactions.summary: A student restates Jiang's account of infernal punishment as a revelation of the sin's consequences, and Jiang condenses the point into the image of a mirror held to the sinner's face.
A long classroom reading moves through Plutus, the hoarders and squanderers, Virgil's discourse on Fortune, and the first sight of the wrathful and sullen in the Styx.

speaker_notes.note: The packet is mostly quoted Dante rather than Jiang's own exposition, but Jiang frames it with the mirror metaphor immediately before the reading starts.

claims.claim: A student correctly tracks Jiang's model of hell by saying the punishment reveals both the principle behind the sin and the damage it does to oneself and others.
claims.temporal_scope: Student synthesis offered during the seminar on 2026-06-21.

claims.claim: Jiang sharpens the seminar's governing image by saying infernal punishment puts a mirror to the sinner's face.
The canto reading presents avarice as a divided economy of hoarding and squandering, dramatized by souls crashing weights into one another while accusing each other of opposite excesses.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Dante passage read in the seminar on 2026-06-21.

claims.claim: The same reading defines Fortune as a providential minister who redistributes worldly goods across peoples and generations beyond ordinary human control.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Dante passage read in the seminar on 2026-06-21.

claims.claim: The packet closes by introducing the Styx as the visible domain of wrath above and sullen bitterness below the waterline.
claims.temporal_scope: Quoted Dante passage read in the seminar on 2026-06-21.

signature_moments.moment: Jiang reduces the whole logic of punishment to a mirror suddenly thrust in front of the sinner.
signature_moments.source_phrase: it's to put a mirror to your face
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of the cleanest formulations yet of his reflective-justice reading of hell.

signature_moments.moment: The hoarders and squanderers eternally collide while shouting opposite accusations.
signature_moments.source_phrase: why do you hoard why do you squander
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The punishment turns economic vice into a repetitive choreography of mutual indictment.

signature_moments.moment: Fortune appears not as chaos but as a hidden sovereign motion humans wrongly curse.
signature_moments.source_phrase: she's the one so frequently maligned even by those who should give praise to her
signature_moments.why_it_matters: It preserves a theological concept Jiang will likely draw on later when discussing order and resentment.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: In the quoted canto, Fortune is the providential minister who shifts worldly goods across peoples and times according to a hidden order.
Jiang's compact frame for hell as an arrangement that makes the sinner see the essence and effects of the sin.

chronology_notes.note: This June 21, 2026 packet binds Jiang's reflective-justice thesis directly to Dante's canto sequence on avarice, Fortune, wrath, and the Styx rather than leaving it as an abstract classroom slogan.

uncertainty_notes.note: The ASR renders Styx-related names noisily, but the transition into the wrathful and sullen is still clear.
